import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Fibonacci Primes

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_prime)
-/

namespace FibonacciPrimes

/--
There are infinitely many Fibonacci primes, i.e., Fibonacci numbers that are prime
It is also a barrier to defining a benchmark from this paper:
https://arxiv.org/html/2505.13938v1 (see Figure 8).

-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem fib_primes_infinite : {n : ℕ | (∃ m : ℕ, m.fib = n) ∧ n.Prime}.Infinite := by
  sorry

/--
There are infinitely many indices $i$, such that the $i$-th Fibonacci is prime.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem fib_primes_infinite.variant : {n : ℕ | n.fib.Prime}.Infinite := by
  sorry

/--
The two ways of phrasing the conjecture are equivalent.
-/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem indices_infinite_iff_fib_primes_infinite : type_of% fib_primes_infinite.variant ↔
    type_of% fib_primes_infinite := by
  simp only [Set.infinite_iff_exists_gt]
  constructor
  · intros h a
    rcases h (a + 1) with ⟨b', ⟨hb₁, hb₂⟩⟩
    use Nat.fib b'
    exact ⟨⟨exists_apply_eq_apply Nat.fib b', hb₁⟩,
      by linear_combination b'.le_fib_add_one + hb₂⟩
  · intro h a
    rcases h (Nat.fib a) with ⟨b', ⟨⟨m, hm⟩, hb₁⟩, hb₂⟩
    use m
    constructor
    · simp_all
    · have := @m.fib_mono a
      omega

end FibonacciPrimes

reformulations.difference: States infinitude of indices n for which Nat.fib n is prime, rather than infinitude of distinct Fibonacci prime values.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Primality of Nat.fib n forces n ≥ 3, and Nat.fib is strictly increasing on indices ≥ 2. Consequently, Nat.fib bijects the prime-valued indices with the Fibonacci prime values. I independently proved the exact infinitude equivalence in /workspace/review/scratch.lean using monotonicity and n ≤ Nat.fib n + 1. The file's own equivalence theorem also has no sorryAx dependency.

sources_consulted: https://arxiv.org/html/2505.13938v1 — Thakur et al., Clever: A Curated Benchmark for Formally Verified Code Generation, Section 2 and Appendix A.2, Figure 8
https://arxiv.org/e-print/2505.13938v1 — checked the relevant LaTeX passages in benchmark_details.tex and appendix.tex
review.notes: Checked all three declarations. Nat.fib has the standard initial conditions and recurrence; indices 0, 1, and 2 yield nonprimes. Lean computations through index 29 match the source's prime values and indices, including index 4. The main predicate is definitionally the intersection of the Fibonacci range with the natural primes. type_of% selects the intended propositions in the equivalence theorem. Both research-open tags agree with the consulted sources.
